concepts.title: Classification of Sources: Owned and Borrowed Funds
concepts.definition: Business finance sources divide into owned funds such as equity shares, retained earnings and venture capital, and borrowed funds such as debentures, loans, public deposits and commercial paper, with period based classification into short, medium and long term.
concepts.key_idea: The choice between debt and equity balances cost, control, risk and financial flexibility for the firm.
question_patterns: classify the sources of business finance on the basis of period
differentiate owned funds and borrowed funds
name the long term sources of finance
which sources provide short term working capital
compare debt and equity as sources of finance
what is meant by financial leverage of borrowed funds

solution_steps.explain: Separate owner funds from creditor funds.
Classify the source by repayment duration.
Compare interest cost with loss of control.

concepts.title: Equity Shares, Preference Shares and Retained Earnings
concepts.definition: Equity shares carry ownership rights, voting power, dividend after preference shares and residual claims, preference shares carry a fixed rate of dividend paid before equity with preferential repayment, and retained earnings are profits reinvested in the business as an internal source called ploughing back of profits.
concepts.key_idea: Equity finance spreads risk among shareholders and needs no repayment, while preference capital is a hybrid of fixed dividend and ownership claim.
concepts.textbook_ref: kebs108.txt shares and retained earnings sections
question_patterns: differentiate equity shares and preference shares

solution_steps.explain: Separate equity holders from preference holders.
Confirm preference dividend comes before equity dividend.
Recognise reinvested profit as retained earnings.

concepts.title: Debentures, Loans and Interest Cost Computation
concepts.definition: Debentures are borrowed fund instruments carrying a fixed rate of interest paid whether or not the firm earns profit, debenture holders being creditors with no voting rights, and the interest cost on borrowed funds is computed as principal multiplied by rate and time.
concepts.key_idea: Interest on debentures is a charge against profit, making borrowed funds cheaper but riskier than equity.
question_patterns: define debentures and state their features
calculate the interest cost of borrowed funds
compare debentures with shares as a source of finance
what is the difference between mortgaged and naked debentures
compute the interest payable on a loan for the given period
why are debenture holders called creditors of the company

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the principal by the rate percent and the years, then divide by 100

concepts.title: Loans from Banks, Public Deposits, Commercial Paper and Trade Credit
concepts.definition: Banks provide term loans and cash credit against security, public deposits invite unsecured deposits from the public for fixed periods, commercial paper is an unsecured short term promissory note of creditworthy companies, and trade credit from suppliers supports working capital needs.
concepts.key_idea: International sources like foreign currency loans, Euro issues and external commercial borrowings supplement domestic sources for large firms.
question_patterns: what are public deposits and their merits
define commercial paper and its features
how does trade credit help working capital
distinguish term loan from cash credit

solution_steps.explain: Note the deposit, note or credit arrangement used.
Separate short term unsecured paper from secured term loans.
Match the source to the working capital or capital expenditure need.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A company issues debentures worth {principal} rupees at {rate_percent} per cent interest for {years} years. Calculate the interest payable for the period.

solution_template.explain: Multiply the principal by the rate percent and the years, then divide by 100

worked_examples.question_pattern: A firm borrows {principal} rupees from a bank at {rate_percent} per cent per annum for {years} years. Find the interest cost of the loan.

solution_template.explain: Multiply the principal by the rate percent and the years, then divide by 100
